comment:purpose: The SHIPPED ingest profile: the closed x_domain and type vocabularies plus the mechanical path→label tables. Data only — the resolution mechanism (longest-prefix-wins, segment-rule override, write-time rejection of an unknown label) lives in src/ingestProfile.ts and does not change with this file.
comment:editing: An unknown domain or type is REFUSED at write time, so a new label MUST be added to `domains`/`types` here before any rule may name it. A missing or malformed file is a hard error — ingest MUST NOT fall back to built-in values. The shipped vocabularies are mirrored as TypeScript unions in src/config.ts and the two are checked equal at load, so a value added here MUST be added there too.
name: default
comment:types: `knowledge` is the FALLBACK, not the norm — the directory an authored document lives in already carries what kind of document it is, so it stays for the sources no rule claims. `research`, `plan` and `lessons-learned` were accepted on write but claimed by NO rule until T2.1, because their real directory names were not settled; the `docs/research/`, `docs/plans/` and `docs/implementation-lessons-learned/` typeRules below are what finally claim them, from the directories the repo actually authors into.
comment:domainRules: Order is PRESENTATION only (narrow roots first, for reading); resolution sorts by prefix length, so `claude-artifacts/` catches everything `claude-artifacts/standards/` does not, and `doc/` everything the ADR root does not. `benchmark-data/cache/bench/corpus-ext/` is a BENCHMARK corpus root holding other projects' published docs, not product knowledge.
comment:typeRules: Same longest-prefix-wins rule: `doc/40-code-standards/90-decisions/` (adr) outranks `doc/40-code-standards/` (standard) by prefix length, not by row order. The external benchmark root types as `vendor-doc` so a type filter alone separates it from authored repo knowledge. The `docs/` rows claim only the subtrees the repo actually authors into; anything else under `docs/` falls to `knowledge`, and `docs/analysis/` types as `review` because its documents ARE reviews under another name.
comment:excludePaths: `docs/` holds 22,808 .md files, and 22,597 of them are machine output: `docs/tmp` (12,211) and `docs/benchmarks` (10,386). Ingesting them buries the ~211 authored documents that are the actual target, so the two generated roots are excluded by path before anything is chunked. `doc/_meta/corpus-digest.md` is excluded as a NAVIGATION artefact, not as generated bulk: it produces 204 atoms and carries one line of vocabulary from every document in the corpus, so it scores on almost any query (observed at rank 2 and rank 5 on unrelated probes). Only that one file — the rest of `doc/_meta/` is authored content and stays. `claude-artifacts/python-init-files/` is excluded as a NESTED DUPLICATE: it holds a second copy of the repo's own `claude-artifacts` tree (26 .md files, including a second `claude-artifacts/standards/FEATURE-FLAG-GOVERNANCE.md`). Because an atom id derives from the source basename plus its heading chain, the duplicate copies generate atom ids that COLLIDE with the canonical `claude-artifacts/standards/` ones, inflating byte-identical dedupe groups, changing which copy survives, and forcing hash-disambiguated ids onto documents that were previously unambiguous. Measured before excluding it: 4 gold judgments unreachable (3 on `FEATURE-FLAG-GOVERNANCE`, 1 on `RESPONSIBILITY-RULES` whose heading still exists in the source but whose atom id gained a hash suffix). After excluding it: 0 unreachable, corpus 14551 → 14391 atoms. The canonical copies remain fully retrievable, so nothing searchable is lost — only the duplicate. `docs/analysis/2026-08-09-1126-adapter-outputs/` is excluded as the SAME class as `docs/benchmarks/`: it holds machine-generated per-query benchmark dumps (adapter output and per-query top-5 id lists) that quote the golden query text verbatim, e.g. an atom titled `Adapter output — linear > q-022 — multi-word-phrase`. Benchmark output must not sit in the corpus the benchmark measures — it matches the benchmark's own queries trivially and outranks the real answers: 250 atoms occupying 188 of 600 top-10 slots (31.3%) across 42 of 60 topics, q-022 had all ten. Measured effect on the corpus-v2 `vault` baseline: nDCG@10 0.4721 → 0.3019 while R@100 barely moved (−0.0082), i.e. gold stayed in the pool and was displaced out of the top 10. Serving was not affected — these atoms type as `review`, which is already in `defaultExcludedTypes` — only the bench, which measures the full corpus by design. It leaves the other ~1126 `docs/analysis/` atoms (authored analysis) in place. Same prefix semantics as domainRules (a repo-relative, forward-slash `startsWith` prefix), so a DIRECTORY prefix carries a trailing slash: `docs/tmp/` cannot silently swallow the sibling `docs/tmpl/`, and `docs/benchmarks/` cannot swallow `docs/benchmarking/` (105 atoms, which survived until now only because the string happened not to match).
comment:defaultExcludedTypes: Owner decision D5, 2026-08-18: 6,475 of 11,345 atoms (57.1%) are history-shaped — a feature log, a benchmark run, a review or a brainstorm — and on the CLI path they drown the authored knowledge a question is asking for. They stay INGESTED and INDEXED and are one flag away; only the default result set leaves them out. CORRECTED 2026-08-22: the second half of this sentence used to read "so the benchmark still measures the FULL corpus and every recorded number stands" and that is FALSE for the DERIVED datasets — `run.ts:typeFilterOf` subtracts this same list from `vault` / `vault-hu` unless `--include-history` is passed, so `vault` derives 6787 of 14706 atoms and every history row stamps `typeFilter`. It remains true of `nfcorpus` / `scifact` / BRIGHT, which are not derived. Recorded numbers still stand — they were all measured under the same filter. handbook/GNOSIS-GUIDE.md § Landmines, `16` § 5 C7. `src/config.ts` reads it into the exported `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_TYPES`, and `src/cli/retrieveCommand.ts` applies that list to an unfiltered CLI `retrieve`; `--exclude-type` REPLACES it and `--include-history` empties it.
comment:defaultPrf: Owner-approved 2026-08-21: RM3 pseudo-relevance feedback is a SERVED default on this profile, at the MEASURED frozen cell fbDocs 10 / fbTerms 40 / alpha 0.5 — the cell `SERVED_PRF_PARAMS` (src/prf.ts) OWNS, and the one the gate was run on (qwen3-reranker-4b: vault-hu nDCG@10 +0.0323 p=0.0186; vault +0.0080 p=0.4567, not significant and adopted deliberately). It is NOT `DEFAULT_PRF_PARAMS`, whose fbTerms is 20 and which no recorded arm used. Like `defaultExcludedTypes` it is a RETRIEVE-TIME default on the CLI path alone: nothing in ingest, the port or an adapter reads it, so the bench still measures the unexpanded first pass and every recorded number stands. `--no-prf` turns it off, and the `--prf-*` flags override one member each.
comment:summarySidecar: Repo-relative path of the SUMMARY SIDECAR — the `source path → summary` table ingest fills a document's `summary:` from. Resolution direction: an in-source `<!-- LLM-PRIMARY: … -->` comment WINS, the sidecar fills in only for a document that declares none, and neither leaves the field absent. That order is what makes the sidecar strictly ADDITIVE: a corpus whose documents still carry their comments ingests byte-identically, so every recorded baseline stands. Its purpose is the corpora this repo does NOT author and may not modify — without the sidecar such a document cannot carry a summary at all. Written by packages/gnosis/scripts/extract-summaries.ts, which walks this profile's own corpus scope; an ABSENT file is the pre-migration state and is read as an empty table, never as an error.
comment:segmentRules: Brainstorms are a SEGMENT rule, not a prefix rule: the directory appears under three unrelated parents, and enumerating those parents would silently mislabel the fourth one somebody adds. Matched on whole path segments, so a directory merely ENDING in the name cannot claim it. A segment rule OVERRIDES every prefix rule.
comment:goldIdsPath: The gold source ingest breaks EXACT-BODY dedupe ties against, named HERE rather than defaulted invisibly: which copy of a byte-identical pair survives decides which SOURCE FILE counts as gold. This is the value the shipped path has always resolved.
